en.g: Etnedalen; a valley in Innlandet, Norway, the valley of the river Etna, running through Etnedal Municipality and continuing into Nordre Land
x: paa begge sider af Etnedalen i Valdres
on both sides of Etnedalen in Valdres

1005022.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse Etnardalr, from the genitive Etnar of the old river name Etn, followed by dalr (“valley”), literally “valley of the Etna”. The modern form has the definite singular ending -en (“definite singular suffix”).
The river name Etn is of uncertain origin. It has been tentatively connected with Old Norse etja (“to urge, drive forward”) or eta (“to eat”).
The valley name was also used as the official name of the municipality created in 1894. By royal resolution of 3 November 1917, the municipality name was changed from Etnedalen to Etnedal, removing the definite ending -en.
